Decree Appointing Liquidating Receiver (Caption.) 

AND NOW, this day of 

19-, upon consideration of the Bill and Answer and upon a hearing and proof of the issues, it is ORDERED and DECREED 1. That be and he is hereby appointed Liquidating Receiver of all the assets, property, franchises, rights, privileges of whatsoever kind of The Company within the jurisdiction of this court, with power to take, hold, demand, receive and collect all of the funds, assets and property belonging to said company or in the hands of any debtor, agent or depository of said company and to account to the court for the same. 

Said receiver is hereby empowered to collect all amounts owing to the company by shareholders on account of any unpaid portion of the consideration for the issuance of shares.

The said receiver is hereby empowered to bring, prosecute and defend all suits at law or in equity in his own

INVOLUNTARY DISSOLUTION 

799 name as receiver of the company which in his judgment may be necessary for the preservation and protection of the property and interests under his name and control. 

The said receiver is hereby empowered, subject to the order of this court, to sell, convey and dispose of all or any part of the assets of the company either at public or private sale.

All creditors of the company are required to file with the receiver proofs under oath of their respective claims prior to the (date shall be not less than four (4) months from the date of the order). Notice of this date shall be given to all creditors and claimants of the company in writing by registered mail to the last known address of the creditor or claimant within ten (10) days from the date hereof. Creditors and claimants failing to file proof of claim on or before the aforesaid date shall be barred from participating in the distribution of the assets of the company.

The said receiver shall file an inventory and appraisement of the property committed to his custody and shall file his account and accounts therefor and shall distribute the same according to law to the persons entitled thereto, with such other powers as may be necessary and incident to protect the rights and interests of all parties in interest. 

2. That upon security being entered by the said receiver in the sum of Dollars ($ -), the defendant company, its agents and employees, are hereby enjoined from taking or retaining possession of the money, or retaining, taking, delivering or assigning any of the assets, property, franchises, rights or privileges of the company, and from collecting or receiving any of the money, assets, securities or property of the company, or in any wise dealing therewith, or in molesting or interfering with the full and absolute possession and control thereof by the said receiver. ARTICLE II. 

Particular Covenants of The Company SECTION 1. Duly and punctually the Company will pay the principal and interest of every debenture issued and secured hereunder without deduction from either principal or interest for any tax or taxes which the Company or the Trustee may be required to pay or to retain therefrom under any present or future law of the United States or of any state or county or municipality therein. 

SECTION 2. Whenever demanded by the Trustee the 

Company will cause to be done, executed, acknowledged and delivered all and every such further acts, deeds, transfers and assurances for the better assuring, conveying and converting unto the Trustee, all and singular, the property hereby conveyed or intended so to be or which the Company herein has covenanted and agreed hereafter to convey to the Trustee as reasonably it shall require, for better accomplishing the provisions and purposes of this Indenture and for securing payment of the principal and interest of the debentures intended to be secured hereby; every such deed, transfer or assurance being intended to be and being supplemental to this Indenture and not an original or independent deed or transfer.

CORPORATIONS SECTION 3. The Company, at an office to be maintained by it in the city of will keep a sufficient register of debentures issued hereunder, which register at all reasonable times shall be open to the inspection of the Trustee, and upon presentation for such purpose it will, under such reasonable regulations as it may prescribe, register therein any of the debentures issued under the provisions hereof. 

Upon presentation at the place where such register is kept of any such registered debenture, bearing a written power to transfer the same, executed by the registered holder for the time being, in a form approved by the Company, such debenture shall be transferred on such register.

The registered holder of any such registered debenture shall also have the right to cause the same to be registered as payable to bearer, in which case transferability by delivery shall be restored and thereafter the principal of such debenture shall be payable to any person presenting the same; but any such debenture registered as payable to bearer may be registered again in the name of the holder with the same effect as a first registration thereof. Successive registrations and transfers as aforesaid may be made from time to time as desired; and each registration of a debenture shall be noted by an officer of the Company or by the Transfer Agent on the debenture. 

Registration of any debenture shall, however, not affect the negotiability of any coupon thereto belonging, but every such coupon shall continue to pass by delivery merely and shall remain payable to bearer. 

In case any debenture issued hereunder or the coupons thereto appertaining shall become mutilated or be destroyed, the Company, in its discretion, may issue and the Trustee thereupon shall certify and deliver a new debenture of like tenor and date, bearing the same serial number, in exchange and substitution for and upon cancellation of the mutilated debenture and its coupons; or in lieu of and substitution for the debenture so destroyed,

SECTION 4. So long as there shall be no default in the payment of the principal or interest of such debentures the Company shall have the right to continue in the possession of the property hereby transferred and to operate the same with like force and effect as if such assignment had not been made, and shall have power from time to time to make such alterations and changes in the property hereby transferred by disposition or otherwise as may be deemed by the Company advisable in carrying on its operations.

SECTION 5. Until all of said debentures shall have been redeemed and retired no dividend exceeding twelve per centum (12%) upon the Common Capital Stock of the Company shall be paid in any year. 

SECTION 6. The Company will not, directly or indirect ly extend or assent to the extension of time for the payment of any of the coupons upon any of said debentures and will not, directly or indirectly, be a party to or approve of any arrangement for such extension by the purchase or keeping alive of any of the coupons for such interest or in any other manner. 

SECTION 7. The Company hereby irrevocably waives all benefit and advantage of any and all valuation, appraisement, stay, exemption and redemption laws now existing or which may hereafter be passed and which, but for this waiver, might be availed of to prevent or to postpone the sale under the terms of this Indenture of the pledged property and franchises, or after sale to permit redemption of the property sold. 

SECTION 8. The Company will properly maintain all property at any time covered by this Indenture, repairing, renewing and replacing the same as may be necessary and will properly operate its plant and preserve the rights, privileges and franchises relating thereto.

CORPORATIONS ARTICLE III Trusts Relating to Pledged Property SECTION 1. Until default is made in the payment of principal or interest due upon said debentures, the Trustee shall not collect any of the property hereby pledged or any moneys due or to become due thereon, but the Company shall be entitled to receive all such moneys. 

SECTION 2. The Trustee may do whatever may in its judgment be necessary for the purpose of maintaining or preserving any of the property hereby pledged, even though no default either in the payment of the principal or interest of said debentures shall have occurred; and in such event the amount of all its necessary and proper expenses and disbursements shall be forthwith paid by the Company to the Trustee upon its demand and if not so paid shall be secured hereby and shall be entitled to payment out of any sale of the property hereby pledged in full, before any payment is made to the holders of said debentures. 

ARTICLE IV Remedies of Trustee and Debenture Holders SECTION 1. No coupon belonging to any debenture is sued hereunder which in any way at or after maturity shall have been transferred or pledged separate or apart from the debenture to which it relates, shall, unless accompanied by such debenture, be entitled in case of default hereunder to any benefit of or from this Indenture except subject to the prior payment in full of the principal of the debentures issued hereunder and of all matured coupons not so transferred or pledged.

SECTION 2. In case the time for payment of any coupons shall have been extended, whether or not such extension be by and with the consent of the Company, such coupons shall not be entitled in case of default hereunder to the benefit or security of this Indenture except subject to the prior payment in full of the principal of all deben-

825 tures issued hereunder then outstanding, and of all matured coupons on such debentures, the payment of which has not been so extended. 

SECTION 3. In case (1) default shall be made in the payment of any coupon or any debenture secured by this Indenture and any such default shall continue for a period of two months; or in case (2) default shall be made in the due and punctual payment of the principal of any debenture hereby secured; or in case (3) default shall be made in the due observance or performance under any other covenant or condition herein required to be kept or performed by the Company, and any such last mentioned default shall continue for a period of two months after written notice thereof from the Trustee or from the holders of twenty-five per centum (25%) in amount of the debentures hereby secured and then outstanding, then and in each such case the Trustee personally or by its agents or attorneys may take possession of the property hereby pledged and sell the same and all moneys due or to become due therefore or thereunder; and all moneys received therefrom shall be applied as follows:

In case the principal of the debentures hereby secured shall not have become due, to the payment of the interest in default in the order of the maturity of the coupons for such interest, together with interest thereon at the rate of six per centum (6%) per annum; such payments to be made ratably to the persons entitled thereto, without discrimination or preference. 

In case the principal of the debentures hereby secured shall have become due, by declaration or otherwise, to the payment first of the interest in default (with interest on the overdue instalments thereof at the rate of six per centum per annum) in the order of the maturity of the coupons for such interest; and, second, to the payment of the principal of all debentures hereby secured; in every instance such payments to be made ratably to the persons entitled thereto without any discrimination or pref erence. 

These provisions, however, not being intended in any wise to modify the provisions of Sections 1 and 2 of this Article IV.

CORPORATIONS 

SECTION 4. In case default shall be made in the payment of any interest on any debenture hereby secured and any such default shall continue for a period of two months, then and in every case of such continuing default, upon the written request of the holders of a majority in amount of the debentures hereby secured then outstanding, the Trustee, by notice in writing delivered to the Company, shall declare the principal of all debentures hereby secured and then outstanding to be due and payable immediately and upon any such declaration the same shall become and be immediately due and payable, anything in this Indenture or in said debentures contained to the contrary notwithstanding. 

This provision, however, is subject to the condition that if at any time after the principal of said debentures shall have been so declared due and payable, all arrears of interest upon said debentures, with interest at the rate of six per centum (6%) per annum on overdue instalments of interest, shall have been paid by the Company or be collected out of the pledged property before any sale of the pledged property shall have been made, then and in every such case, the holders of a majority in amount of the debentures hereby secured then outstanding, by written notice to the Company and to the Trustee, may waive such default and its consequences; but no such waiver shall extend to or affect any subsequent default or impair any right consequent thereon. 

SECTION 5. ARTICLE V 

Immunity of Officers, Directors and Shareholders No recourse under or upon any obligation, covenant or agreement of this Indenture, or of any debenture or coupon hereby secured, or because of the creation of any indebtedness hereby secured shall be had against any incorporator, shareholder, officer or director of the Company, or of any successor corporation either directly or through the Company by the enforcement of any assessment or by any legal or equitable proceeding by virtue of any statute or otherwise; it being expressly agreed and understood that this Indenture and the obligations hereby secured are solely corporate obligations and that no personal liability whatever shall attach to, or be incurred by the incorporators, shareholders, officers or directors of the Company, or to any successor corporation, or any of them because of the incurring of the indebtedness hereby authorized, or under or by reason of any of the obligations, covenants or agreements contained in this Indenture, or in any of the debentures or coupons hereby secured or implied therefrom; and that any and all personal liability of every name and nature either at common law or in equity, or by statute or by constitution, of any and all rights and claims against every such shareholder, officer or director are hereby expressly waived as a condition of and as a consideration for, the execution of this Indenture and the issue of such debentures and interest obligations.

847 the action of the Voting Trustees and shall have the same effect as if assented to by all. The Voting Trustees may adopt their own rules of procedure. 

Seventh. In voting the stock held by them the Voting 

Trustees shall exercise their best judgment from time to time to select suitable directors to the end that the affairs of the Company shall be properly managed. They shall have the right to elect themselves or any of them, directors of said company. In voting upon any matters which may come before them at any shareholders' meeting, Voting Trustees will exercise their like best judgment; but they shall incur no liability or responsibility of any sort with respect to any action taken pursuant to any votes cast by them. No Voting Trustee shall be held liable for any error of law, or by reason of any matter or thing done or omitted under this agreement, except for his own individual malfeasance.

Eighth. Voting Trustees will not during the pendency of this agreement vote with respect to the shares of the capital stock of the Company held by them to authorize any additional mortgage upon the property of the said

Company, nor to create any obligation or indebtedness that will prejudice the rights of the holders of said Trust Certificates, nor to authorize any increase in the amount of the stock of the said Company, except with the consent in each instance of the holders of a majority of the whole amount of the Trust Certificates for said stock, as expressed in writing by the owners of the said Trust Certificates assenting hereto. 

Ninth. At or before the expiration of the term of years from the date hereof, the persons then holding and owning Trust Certificates representing not less than a majority of all the shares of stock of the Company then issued and outstanding, may by an instrument in writing duly signed, continue the existence of this Voting Trust for a further period of five years, or any less period.

Tenth. This agreement shall not be valid or binding

CORPORATIONS 

upon any of the shareholders, parties of the first part hereto, until and unless it is signed by shareholders owning not less than seventy-five per centum (75%) of the stock of the

Company now issued and outstanding. 

Eleventh. During the continuance of this trust the certificates for the shares of stock held by the Voting Trustees under the terms thereof shall be deposited with the 

Trust Company, of which shall also act as registrar of the Trust Certificates. 

Twelfth. This agreement may be simultaneously executed in several counterparts, each of which when so executed shall be deemed to be an original and such counterparts shall together constitute but one and the same instrument.

In witness whereof, Shareholders and Voting Trustees have hereunto set their hands and seals, and the Trust Company has caused its corporate seal to be hereto affixed, duly attested by the signatures of its president and secretary, the day and year first above written.

34. By-Laws ARTICLE I 

Shareholders 

SECTION 1. Certificates of stock shall be issued to the shareholders and transfers made when required, said certificates to be signed by the President or Vice-President and the Treasurer, registered by the Secretary, and authenticated by the seal of the Company. 

SEC. 2. The stock of the Company shall be transferred only on the books of the Company by the shareholders himself in person, or by his attorney in fact, duly constituted, according to such forms as the Directors may prescribe. The certificates surrendered shall be canceled at time of transfer, and filed with the Treasurer of the Company.

SEC. 3. No transfers of stock shall be made upon the books of the Company for days preceding the date appointed for the payment of any dividend or for any election. Only those persons who appear on the books of the Company as shareholders shall be entitled to receive any dividends or to vote at any meeting or election of the Company.

SEC. 4. Any person or persons desiring a certificate of stock to be issued in lieu of one lost or destroyed, shall, after applying for the same, advertise such loss or destruction in one or more newspapers published in Pennsylvania, twice a week for four weeks, stating the number and date of the certificate lost or destroyed, the number of shares represented thereby, and that application has been made to the Board of Directors for a cer-

CORPORATIONS 

tificate in lieu thereof. The applicant shall then furnish the Board of Directors with an affidavit describing the certificate, its loss or destruction, and advertisement made in conformity therewith, accompanied by a copy of the advertisement, and also a bond of indemnity, with satisfactory personal security, in at least double the amount of the certificate, against any damage that may arise from issuing a new certificate; whereupon the 

Board may direct (one month after the date of appearance of the last advertisement) the issue of a new certificate, of the same tenor with the one alleged to be lost or destroyed, therein specifying that it is in lieu thereof. 

And the application for a new certificate, and the evidence of compliance by the applicant with all the requirements of this by-law, shall be made in such form as shall be satisfactory to the Board of Directors. 

SEC. 5. Each shareholder, at the time of the issuance to him of a stock certificate, shall notify the Secretary in writing of the address to which he wishes notices relating to the business of the Company to be mailed to him. He shall thereafter notify the Secretary of any change in such address.

SEC. 6. The general office of the Company, and also the offices of the President, of the Secretary and of the Treasurer, with the books and papers thereto belonging, shall be at Pennsylvania.

ARTICLE II Meetings of Shareholders SECTION 1. The annual meeting of the shareholders shall be held at the general office of the Company, or at such other place as the Board of Directors may provide, on the in each year, unless that day be duly designated a legal holiday, in which event the annual meeting shall be held on the following day not a legal holiday. day of

SEC. 2. At the annual meeting of the shareholders there

BY-LAWS 

859 shall be held an election for Directors to serve for the ensuing year, or until their successors be chosen, which election shall be conducted by the judges appointed by the Board of Directors and duly qualified as required by law.

SEC. 3. Special meetings of the shareholders may be called at any time upon the written request of a majority of the Board of Directors; or any shareholder or shareholders holding at least one-tenth in amount of the capital stock of the Company, may at any time apply to the President, or, in his absence, to the Secretary, to call a special meeting of the shareholders; and upon such application, which shall state the object of the meeting, it shall be the duty of the President, or in his absence, the Secretary, to call such meeting within thirty days from date of receipt of the application. 

SEC. 4. At least (10-60) days' notice shall be given of the time when and place where the annual or any special meeting of the shareholders is to be held. Such notice shall be signed by the Secretary of the Company and mailed to each shareholder at the address last given by him, as herein provided. If no such address be given, notice deposited in the post office, addressed to him at the city in which the general office of the Company is located, shall be sufficient. 

SEC. 5. The notice of every special meeting shall state briefly the special business to come before the meeting, and only such business shall be considered at such meeting, unless with the consent of shareholders holding three-fourths of the entire capital stock of the Company. 

SEC. 6. A roll of the shareholders in alphabetical order, together with the last address given and the number of shares held by each shareholder, shall be kept by the Secretary and laid before the shareholders at each of their meetings. Such list shall always be open to the examination of any shareholder at the office of the Company. 

SEC. 7. At all shareholders' meetings shareholders may

CORPORATIONS 

attend and vote either in person or by proxy. All proxies shall be in writing. Partnerships may sign in the name of the partnership, and the signature of the firm by any member thereof shall be valid. No proxy shall be valid for more than (11 mos.) from the date thereof.

SEC. 8. The holders for the time being of a majority of the outstanding shares of stock of the Company, appearing either in person or by proxy, shall constitute a quorum for the transaction of business at any annual or special meeting of the shareholders; but the holders of a less number, appearing at the time and place for which such meeting was called may adjourn from time to time for a period not exceeding twenty days. 

SEC. 9. All elections shall be by ballot, unless by unanimous consent the vote be taken viva voce. When by ballot, the record of the name of, and amount of stock represented by, each party voting shall be made and certified to by judges, duly appointed, and shall be kept on file with the archives of the Company, and in case of an election for any officer of the Company elected by the stockholders, a report of the result thereof shall be in like manner made, certified to, and filed. 

SEC. 10. Each Director shall be a shareholder in the 

Company, and shall hold his office, unless removed or disqualified from some cause, until the next stated annual meeting, and thereafter until his successor shall be chosen.

SEC. 11. The shareholders of the Company may, by a vote of three-fourths of all the stock, at any meeting duly convened and called for the purpose, remove any one or more of the Directors or other officers of the Company, and may then proceed to fill the vacancy or vacancies caused by such removal or removals. 

ARTICLE III 

Directors 

SECTION 1. The number of the Directors of the Com pany shall be 

The Secretary and Treasurer of

BY-LAWS 

861 the Company shall be ex officio Secretary and Treasurer of the Board of Directors. 

SEC. 2. The first regular meeting of the Board of Di rectors shall be held each year immediately upon the adjournment of the meeting of the shareholders in that year at which the Directors are elected. Regular meetings of the Board of Directors shall also be held at the general office of the Company, on the day of each month, unless otherwise designated by the Board. Meetings may be called at any other time by the President, and shall be called by him, or, in his absence, by the Secretary, on the written request of three members of the Board, to be convened at such time and place as may be appointed. 

A majority of the Board shall constitute a business quorum.

SEC. 3. At the first regular meeting of the Board of 

Directors after their election, they shall elect a President, Vice-President, Secretary and Treasurer of the Company to serve for the ensuing year and thereafter until their successors shall be chosen. The President shall be and each other officer may be, a Director of the Company. Any two of said offices may be held by the same person.

SEC. 4. The President shall preside at all meetings of the Board of Directors, preserve order and regulate debates according to parliamentary rules, and appoint all committees not otherwise ordered by the Board. In the absence of the President, the Vice-President shall preside. In the absence of both President and Vice-President, a President pro tempore may be appointed by the 

Board.

SEC. 6. The Board of Directors shall have power, for sufficient cause, to remove from an office or position, other than that of Director, any officer, agent or employee of the Company by a vote of a majority of the entire Board, and shall have power to fill the vacancies so occurring or created, and for the purpose of filling any vacancy, a vote of the majority of the whole Board shall be sufficient.

SEC. 7. The Board of Directors may, by a vote of a majority of the Board, accept the resignation of any one or more of its members, or of any officer or officers of the Company, and have power forthwith to fill the vacancy or vacancies, so created, by the election of a successor or successors to such resigning member or members, or officer or officers of the Company. But if the officer so resigning be an officer elected by the shareholders, a special meeting of the shareholders shall be forthwith called, to convene within thirty days, to hold an election to fill the vacancy.

SEC. 8. The Board of Directors shall fix the compensa tion of the officers and agents of the Company and the wages of other employees.

SEC. 9. The Board of Directors may appoint from their own number an Executive Committee, who shall serve during the pleasure of the Board, and to whom may be intrusted by the Board such business as may be lawfully delegated to such a committee. The Executive Committee shall report promptly to the Board all actions taken by it. Vacancies therein shall be filled by the Board. 

ARTICLE IV 

Officers 

SECTION 1. The President shall be a shareholder and 

Director of the Company and shall hold a vigilant superintendence over all the affairs of the Company, and shall

BY-LAWS 

863 have general supervision and control of all the employees of the Company, and shall prescribe their duties when not otherwise provided for. 

He shall have custody of the seal of the Company, and attend generally to its executive business, under the direction of the Board, and be ex officio a member of all committees.

All letters, reports or other papers relating to the business of the Company, received by the Secretary or by the Treasurer, shall be submitted to the President, and when practicable, all instructions emanating from either of those officers shall be first approved by the President or by the Board of Directors. 

SEC. 2. The Vice-President shall be a shareholder of the Company, and shall, in the absence or disability of the President perform his duties. He shall also perform any of the duties imposed by these by-laws on the President which the President may delegate or the Board of Directors may assign to him. 

SEC. 3. The Secretary shall be present at all meetings of the shareholders and the Board, take minutes of the proceedings, and record the same in a suitable book for preservation. He shall notify the members of all regular and called meetings of the Board, and furnish the chairman of each committee with a copy of the resolution appointing such committee, and shall perform all duties which are imposed on him by these by-laws or are customary and incident to the office of Secretary in like corporations.

He shall have charge of the books, maps, letters, deeds, &c., in the office of the Company. 

SEC. 4. The Treasurer shall give bonds, with one or more satisfactory sureties, in such sum as the Board may from time to time require, for the faithful performance of all his duties. The cost of procuring such bonds shall be defrayed by the Company. 

He shall keep a regular set of books, containing the 28

CORPORATIONS 

accounts of the Company, and of all the funds that may pass through his hands.

He shall make reports of his receipts and disbursements at each regular meeting of the Board of Directors, in such form and detail as the Board may direct; shall present a complete statement of his accounts for the previous fiscal year, at the meeting of the Board immediately preceding the annual meeting of the shareholders; and shall attend to such other duties as the President or the Board of Directors may from time to time require. 

His books shall at all times be open to the inspection of the President, the Vice-President or any member of the 

Board. 

The money of the Company shall be deposited by the Treasurer in such bank or banks or other depository as the Directors of the Company may from time to time prescribe. No money deposited in any bank or other depository to the Company's credit shall be withdrawn, except upon a check executed in such a way as the Board of Directors may from time to time prescribe, or by vouchers duly signed in such form as may be approved by the Board of Directors. 

SEC. 5. No officer, agent or employee of the Company shall have power to make, indorse or accept any draft, promissory note, bill of exchange or other instrument for the payment of money in the name or on behalf of the Company, except for the purposes of its usual business or when specially authorized by a majority of the Board of Directors. All such instruments shall be signed on behalf of the Company in the manner provided in these by-laws in the case of checks. But any such instrument may be indorsed in the name of the Company for deposit in bank or for collection on its behalf by any officer of the Company.

SEC. 6. In addition to the officers elected by the shareholders and the Board of Directors, there may be appointed by the President such other officers and agents as may, in his judgment, be deemed necessary for the

STOCK CERTIFICATE 

865 effective transaction of the business of the Company, subject to the approval of the Board at the next meeting subsequent to such appointment.

ARTICLE VI Amendments 

These by-laws may be amended at any regular or special meeting of the shareholders; but no alteration or amendment shall be made in them unless notice in writing, stating the terms of the proposed amendment, has been given to the Secretary at least thirty days before the date of such meeting, and notice has been sent, at least fifteen days before such meeting, to each shareholder at the address last given by him to the Secretary, setting out in full the existing by-law and the proposed amendment thereto. It shall be the duty of the Secretary to send such notice to the shareholders; but such notice may be sent by the shareholder proposing the amendment.

35. Specific Purposes

Abattoir 

To slaughter cattle, sheep and hogs, to pack and preserve meats, to manufacture and deal in tallow, lard and kindred products, to manufacture the offal of animals into merchantable products and sell the same, to cure and deal in hides, pelts and skins and generally to carry on and transact such other business in connection with said branches of business above named as is usually or may profitably be so carried on and transacted. Accountants The business to be done by this corporation is to employ bookkeepers and auditors and accountants for hire to serve clients; to keep, examine, audit, analyze accounts and records of individuals, partnerships, and corporations; to install systems of bookkeeping and accounts and in general to do a general bookkeeping business for hire as service to clients.

Advertising That the purpose for which said corporation is formed is to carry on the business of promotion and sale of all kinds of advertising service, and generally to conduct

CORPORATIONS 

Me all lines of business allied to and interdependent with that of advertising and advertising service.

Airships and Motor Vehicles 

The business to be done by this corporation is to manufacture, buy, and sell and assemble, repair, store, hire, rent, operate and deal in and with aeroplanes of all kinds, and parts thereof, and supplies therefor, and all articles and things pertaining thereto, or the operation thereof. 

And to manufacture, buy sell, rent, hire, assemble, repair, and store motor vehicles and airships of all kinds and parts therefor, and to deal in all kinds of motor vehicles and airship parts and supplies.

And to do any and all things incidental to and necessary to the operation of an airship company and an aeroplane company, engaged in manufacturing and selling the same and instructing persons in the operation thereof.

Apartment Houses 

To purchase, lease or otherwise acquire real estate necessary to the operations of the company; to buy, lease, build, erect, equip, operate, maintain and sell apartment houses and residence hotels; to purchase, lease, install and operate furnaces, boilers and machinery, to supply heat, steam, water, electricity and other means for heating, lighting, power signaling and other purposes; to construct, install, lease, own and operate telephone exchanges in buildings owned or operated. 

Athletic Club 

For the purpose of amusement and the promotion of athletics among its members by promoting and participating in games, not for profit, but conducive to physical and mental development and the amusement of its members and for the purpose of acquiring and holding a club house and other necessary paraphernalia and necessary

SPECIFIC PURPOSES 

869 property to be used in futhering the purposes of this association. 

Automobiles-Garage and Agency 

To engage in buying and selling automobiles, automotive accessories; to act as agent for manufacturers of automobiles and accessories and to negotiate the purchase and sale of automobiles as agents as well as to operate and conduct a general garage and to do all things incidental thereto. 

Bonds and Mortgages 

To buy, sell, hold and generally to deal in real estate mortgages of all kinds, real estate mortgage bonds, chattel mortgages, conditional sales contracts, any and all evidences of indebtedness secured by real estate or chattels of any kind, and to deal generally in bonds, debentures, mortgages and securities of all kinds, to borrow money, to make loans and to advance money on contracts; and to do any and all things incidental to and necessary for the conduct of a general business dealing in bonds, mortgages and secured loans. Boom Companies Said corporation is formed for the purpose of constructing dams, and the driving and floating of saw-logs, timber and lumber, on the in the county of a stream not exceeding thirty-five miles in length, with the right to purchase dams, and erect and maintain new dams on said stream, and to clear out, straighten, deepen, crib and widen said stream. 

Bridge or Ferry Companies

Building and Construction

15.

Merger and Consolidation 

A. JOINT PLAN OF MERGER OR CONSOLIDATION 

Before the application is made to the court, a joint plan of merger or consolidation, as the case may be, setting forth the terms and conditions of the merger or consolidation and such other details and provisions as are deemed necessary, shall be approved by the affirmative vote of at least a majority of the members of each of the merging or consolidating corporations entitled to vote thereon, at a regular or special meeting of each corporation convened after at least ten days' written notice to all the members of this purpose. The fact of such approval shall be certified on the joint plan by the secretary of each corporation, and the plan so adopted and certified shall be signed and acknowledged by two duly authorized officers of each corporation.

(Date.) COVENANTS AND RESTRICTIONS See BONDS; DEEDS; LEASES; MORTGAGES 

A COVENANT is an agreement between two or more persons, entered into in writing and under seal, whereby either party stipulates for the truth of certain facts, or promises to perform or give something to the other, or to abstain from the performance of certain things. 

In a promise or contract not under seal, a consideration must be shown; in a covenant under seal, no consideration is necessary to give it validity, even in a court of equity.

The general requisites to a covenant are, 1st, proper parties; 

2dly, an agreement; 3dly, a legal promise; and 4thly, that it be properly executed. 

1st. The parties must be such as by law can enter into a contract. If, either for want of understanding [as in the case of an idiot or lunatic; or in the case of an infant (under 21 years of age) where the contract is not for his benefit]; or where there is understanding, but, owing to certain causes [as coverture, in the case of a married woman (except where Acts of Assembly have conferred power upon the wife), or duress, in every case], the parties are not competent, they cannot bind themselves. 

2dly. There must be an agreement. The assent or consent must be mutual; for the agreement would be incomplete if either party withheld his assent to any of its terms. The assent to the contract necessarily supposes a free, fair, serious exercise of the reasoning faculty. Now, if from any cause, this free assent be not given, the contract is void. 

3dly. A covenant against any positive law, or public policy, is generally void. As an example of the first is a covenant by one man that he will rob another; and of the last, a covenant by a merchant or tradesman that he will not follow his occupation or calling. This, if it be unlimited, is absolutely void; but if the covenant be that he shall not pursue his business in a particular place, as that he will not trade in the City of Philadelphia, the covenant is no longer against public policy. A covenant to do an impossible thing is also void. 

4thly. To make a covenant, it must, according to the definition above given, be by deed, or under seal. The law does not seem to have appropriated any set of words as absolutely required in creating a covenant. Any words which manifest the intention of the parties to perform an act are sufficient. In 

Pennsylvania it is declared by statute that the words grant, bargain, and sell," shall amount to a covenant that the grantor was seized of an estate in fee, free from all encumbrances done or suffered by him, and for quiet enjoyment against his acts. 

But it has been adjudged that those words in the Pennsylvania statute of 1715 did not amount to a general warranty, but merely to a covenant that the grantor had not done any act, nor created any encumbrance whereby the estate might be defeated. 

Section 3 of the Act of 1 April, 1909, P. L. 91, provides that, in any deed thereafter executed, the words "grant and convey," 66

or either of said words, "shall be adjudged an express covenant to the grantee, his heirs and assigns; to wit, That the grantor was seized of an indefeasible estate in fee simple in the property conveyed, freed from incumbrances done or suffered from the grantor, as also for quiet enjoyment against the grantor, hist heirs and assigns, unless limited by express words contained in said deed." Section 4 provides that a covenant by the grantor that he "will warrant generally the property hereby conveyed" shall have the same effect as a covenant of general warranty written out in full. And Section 5 provides that the words "will warrant specially the property hereby conveyed" shall have the same effect as a covenant of special warranty. 

Covenants are express or implied. 1st An express covenant, or a covenant in fact, is one expressly agreed. between the parties and inserted in the deed. The law does not require any particular form to create an express covenant. The formal word "covenant" is therefore not indispensably requisite. The words, "I oblige," "agree," or, "I bind myself to pay so much such a 'day, and so much such another day," are held to be covenants; and so are the words of a bond. But words importing merely an order or direction that other persons should pay a sum of money are not a covenant.

A covenant in law, is one which the law intends and implies, though it be not expressed in words. There are some words which of themselves do not import an express covenant, yet, being made use of in certain contracts, have a similar operation, and are called covenants in law. They are as effectually binding on the parties as if expressed in the most unequivocal terms. A few examples will fully explain this. If a lessor demise and grant to his lessee a house or lands for a certain term, the law will imply a covenant on the part of the lessor that the lessee shall during the term quietly enjoy the same against all encumbrances. And the words "yielding and paying” in a lease imply a covenant, on the part of a lessee, that he will pay the rent. 

1. General Form of a Covenant by One Person 

And the said John Jones, for himself, his heirs, executors, and administrators, [or as the case may require], doth hereby covenant to and with the said William Burns,

COVENANTS 

911 his heirs, executors, administrators, and assigns, [or as the case may require], by these presents, as follows; that, &c. [here insert whatever is agreed upon]. 

2. General Form of a Covenant by Two or More Persons 

Jointly and Severally And the said John Jones and John Doe, for themselves, their heirs, executors, and administrators, [or as the case may require], do hereby jointly and severally covenant to and with the said William Burns, his heirs, executors, administrators, and assigns, [or as the case may require], by these presents, as follows [here insert whatever is agreed upon]. 

3. Covenant by a Husband for Himself and Wife 

And the said John Jones, for himself, his heirs, executors, and administrators, and for and on behalf of the said Mary Jones, and her heirs, executors, and administrators, doth covenant with the said William Burns, his heirs, executors, administrators, and assigns, as follows; that, &c. [here insert agreement].

Confines His Covenant to His Own Portion of an Estate And the said John Jones, for himself, his heirs, executors, and administrators, for the estate, right, title, quiet enjoyment, and further assurance of one-sixth part of the said hereditaments and premises; and the said John 

Doe, for himself, his heirs, executors, and administrators, for the estate, right, title, quiet, enjoyment, and further assurance of one-sixth part of the said hereditaments and premises; and the said [here continue to state the remainder of the parties in the same way as the first two above] do, and each and every of them doth, severally, but not jointly, covenant, each for himself and his heirs, with the said William Burns, his heirs, executors, administrators, and assigns that, [here state what is covenanted].

S., his heirs and assigns in manner following, viz. that for the purpose of affording light and air to the said hereby granted premises, no building, part of a building, or other obstructions whatever, of a greater height than feet from the level of the ground, shall at any time hereafter be erected upon that part of the said lot of ground of feet in breadth, (adjoining the said hereby granted premises on the -), which lies between a line running parallel with and feet eastward from street, and a line running parallel with and feet westward from street aforesaid, except only the eaves [and such other exceptions as the case may require]. 

16. Covenant Restricting the Type of Building, &c. 

It is expressly covenanted and agreed by and between the parties hereto that no building other than one dwelling house to cost not less than $shall ever be erected upon the within described premises nor shall such building approach the front building line nearer than feet, nor the side lines of said lot nearer than feet, except that bay windows or steps may extend for a distance of feet from the lines as hereby established.

18. Covenant that Lessee May Deduct Out of His Rent the Amount Paid by Him for Taxes and Repairs 

And also that it shall and may be lawful, to and for the said William Burns, his executors, administrators, and assigns, to retain, deduct, and keep out of every year's rent, agreed to be paid to the said John Jones, his heirs or assigns, as aforesaid, so much money as he, the said William Burns, his executors, administrators, or assigns, shall from time to time, during the said term, have paid for taxes on said premises, or such repairs, amendments, and additions by him made or done, or cause to be made or done, in and about said premises, by and with the consent or direction of the said John Jones, his heirs or assigns; or for repairs to said premises without the direction or consent of the said John Jones, his heirs or assigns, provided said repairs are necessary to keep the said premises in proper tenantable condition. 

19. Covenant that Lessee Shall Pay Taxes

That he, the said William Burns, his executors, administrators, and assigns, shall and will from time to time, and at all times, during the said term hereby granted, well and truly pay, in addition to the sum hereinbefore named for rent, all rates, taxes, in excess of those for the current year, [or as the case may be], duties, charges, and assessments whatsoever, that shall or may be assessed, charged, rated, or imposed on the said hereby demised premises, or any part thereof, and thereof and therefrom save harmless and keep indemnified the said John Jones, his executors, administrators, and assigns; and also his and their lands and tenements.

20. Covenant that Lessor Shall Insure the Premises against Fire and Rebuild in Case of Destruction or 

Damage by Fire. 

And that he, the said John Jones, his executors, administrators, and assigns, shall and will, at his and their own proper costs and charges, from time to time sufficiently insure all and every the messuages or tenements, erections or buildings which shall be erected and built upon the said piece or parcel of ground hereby demised, or any part thereof, from casualties by fire, during the then remainder of the said term hereby granted, in some one or more of the public offices kept for that purpose in Philadelphia; and in case the said messuages or tenements, erections or buildings, or any of them, or any part of them, shall at any time or times during the said term be burnt down, destroyed, or damaged by fire, shall and will immediately afterwards rebuild, or well and sufficiently repair the same." 

21. Covenant that Lessee Shall Not Be Chargeable for

Any Accident by Fire 

It is covenanted, concluded, and agreed, by and between the said parties to these presents, that the said lessee, his executors, administrators, or assigns, shall not by virtue of these presents, or any article, clause or agreement herein contained, be chargeable or charged with, or answerable for any accidents of fire which shall happen during the continuance of this demise, and that such accidents of fire are wholly excepted out of the before mentioned covenants for keeping and leaving the premises in repair; and the said lessee, his executors, administrators, and assigns are not by color of any clause in these presents contained, to answer or make good any such accidents or any damage occasioned thereby, but that the same are to be borne by the said lessor, his heirs *A provision may be inserted that if the necessary repairs cannot be made within a specified time the lease may be terminated by one or both parties thereto.

DECEDENTS' ESTATES (See ACCOUNTS; DEEDS; EQUITY; FIDUCIARIES; WILLS) PRELIMINARY NOTE 

On October 4, 1915, pursuant to authority granted him by the Act of April 23, 1915, P. L. 177, the Governor appointed three 

Commissioners "to codify and revise the law of decedents' estates." 

The suggestions contained in their report, submitted on February 1, 1917, have been incorporated in the following acts of June 7, 1917: 

Intestate Act, P. L. 429. 

Partition Act, P. L. 337. 

Fiduciaries Act, P. L. 447. 

Revised Price Act, P. L. 388.

Wills Act, P. L. 403. 

Register of Wills Act, P. L. 415. 

Orphans' Court Act, P. L. 363. 

It necessarily follows that the practice and forms used in practice have been changed considerably. The editors have herein revised all the forms in the last edition and brought them to date so as to eliminate the necessity of reference to any other book of forms on the particular subject. Citations to the acts have been appended to the forms where deemed necessary. 

The jurisdiction of the Orphans' Court now includes trusts inter vivos and life insurance trusts by virtue of the amendment of 26 June, 1931 P. L. 1384.

Terms of the Orphans' Court of Philadelphia County have been abolished.

2. On April 8, 19—, a certain paper writing, dated the 18th day of March, 19—, a copy of which is hereto annexed, alleged to be the last will and testament of the said decedent, was admitted to probate by the Register of Wills of Philadelphia County, and Letters Testamen tary thereon were issued to H. S., G. S. and F. V., the 

Executors therein named. 

3. That on the second day of November, 19—, your petitioner filed his appeal from the judicial act or decision of the Register of Wills in admitting the said alleged will to probate, and duly entered the security required by the Act of Assembly, and the record of the proceedings before the Register has been duly certified by him and filed in this Court. 

4. Your petitioner verily believes, and expects to be able to prove that the said decedent, at the time of the execution of the alleged will, was not of sound disposing mind, memory and understanding, but on the contrary, was of unsound mind, and incompetent to execute any paper requiring the exercise of discretion, mind, memory or understanding, and that the execution of the said alleged will was procured by the contrivance and undue influence of the said F. V., one of the executors therein named, and of others whom your petitioner is at this time unable to name with precision. The facts and circumstances upon which your petitioner bases his belief are as follows:

The decedent was upwards of seventy-nine years of age at the time of the date of the execution of the said alleged will, and was suffering from arterio sclerosis, and chronic nephritis. He was eccentric to a degree indicating unsoundness of mind. Up to the date of his death, the relations between him and your petitioner and his other nephews and nieces were pleasant, and he had intimated that it was his intention to leave his estate, or at least a large portion of it to them. I am informed that the value of his estate is upwards of two hundred thousand dollars ($200,000). By the paper which has been admitted to probate as his will, he gives to various relations legacies aggregating ten thousand dollars ($10,000) to various charities, legacies aggregating eighteen thousand dollars, ($18,000), and the entire residue of his estate to the Society. H. S., G. S. and F. V., who are the executors named in the will, are all members of the said Society, and the said F. V., for a number of years prior to the decedent's death and at the time of the execution of the alleged will, had entire charge of the decedent's affairs. 

5. The names of the parties in interest are, L. T., A. S., C. H., A. W., A. H., The Society, [et., etc.], all of whom are named as legatees in said alleged will; H. S., G. S. and F. 10. Precept to Common Pleas ss: 

COUNTY OF THE COMMONWEALTH OF PENNSYLVANIA 

To the Judges of the Court of Common Pleas of the said 

County, Greeting: 

J. day of 

Whereas, A. B., on the in the year, et cetera, presented to G. H., our Register of Wills of said county, for probate, a certain writing hereto annexed, purporting to have been made the day of in the year, et cetera (or otherwise describing the paper in question), which said writing the said A. B. avers is the last will and testament of the said C. D.; and whereas, E. D., who is a son and heir of the said C. D. (or intermarried with F. D., who is a daughter and heir, et cetera, according to the fact), hath objected before our said Register that the said writing was procured by duress and constraint (stating the matters of fact objected); and

Whereas, our said register hath admitted (or refused to admit) said writing to probate as the last will and testament of the said C. D.; and whereas, the said E. D. hath appealed from the decree of our said register to our Orphans' Court for the said county (or, as the case may be): and

DECEDENTS' ESTATES 

Whereas, the said E. D. (or A. B.) hath requested that an issue may be directed into our said Court of Common Pleas, to try by a jury the validity of the said writing, and the matters of fact which may be objected thereto in our said court:

Therefore, we command you that you cause an action to be entered upon the records of our said court, as of the day of the delivery of this our precept into the office of the prothonotary of our said court, between the said A. B. and the said E. D., so that an issue therein may be formed upon the merits of the controversy between the said parties, and tried in due course according to the practice of our said courts in actions commenced by writ: 

Further, that you cause all other persons who may be interested in the estate of the said C. D., as heirs, relations, or next of kin, devisees, legatees, or executors, to be warned, so that they may come into our said court and become party to the said action, if they shall see cause; and that you certify the result of the trial, so had in the premises, into our said Orphans' Court. 

Attest: 

President Judge of the Orphans' Court of the said county.

10. Petition for Widows' or Children's Allowance in 

Estates of Less Than $500 (Where the decedent leaves an estate not exceeding $500.00, the widow or children may be allowed an exemption of $500.00 without notice of appraisement or the Court may appoint two appraisers. If the petition is for minor children it may be presented by the next friend or guardian.) 

G. THE $5,000 ALLOWANCE 

(In cases of intestacy, there being no issue, the surviving spouse is entitled to $5,000 (in addition to the $500 exemption) taken from the real or personal estate, in addition to one-half of the balance of the estate. 

Act 1917, P. L. 429, Section 2a. This petition must be filed in the county in which the real estate lies. Where that is not the county in which the decedent was domiciled the petition must be authorized by the Orphans' Court of the latter county unless it is outside of the Commonwealth in which case no authorization is necessary; Act of 25 June, 1931, P. L. 1373.)

11. Precept to Common Pleas 

PHILADELPHIA COUNTY SS: 

THE COMMONWEALTH OF PENNSYLVANIA 

To the Judges of the Court of Common Pleas of the said 

County, Greeting: 

WHEREAS, A dispute upon a matter of fact has arisen before our Orphans' Court, in the estate of John Doe, as to the validity of a certain promissory note dated May 17, 1906, for $2,500, alleged to have been made by the decedent, and upon which is founded a claim by John Smith against the estate of said decedent; and 

WHEREAS, We deem it expedient to send said issue to our court of common pleas for the trial of facts by jury; therefore 

WE COMMAND You that you cause an action to be entered upon the records of our said court of common pleas, as of the day of the delivery of this our precept into the office of the prothonotary of our said court, between John Smith as plaintiff, and John Jones, executor of the last will and testament of John Doe, deceased, as defendant, so that an issue therein may be formed upon the merits of the controversy between the said parties, and tried in due course according to the practice of our said courts in actions commenced by writ, to determine the following question of fact:

DECEDENTS' ESTATES 

Is the signature to the original note, a copy of which herein appears, the genuine signature of John Doe, deceased? 

[Copy of note.] 

And further, that said issue be tried, without further pleading, in all respects, as if the plaintiff had duly issued a writ against said defendant and the same had been duly served, and duly filed and served a statement of claim setting forth a copy of said promissory note, and had averred therein that the sum of $2,500 represented by said note was justly due and owing to plaintiff, with interest from May 16, 1920, and the defendant had duly filed and served an affidavit denying that said note was duly made and executed by the decedent and alleging said signature to said note was a forgery, and denying that the said claim of the plaintiff founded upon said note was a valid and lawful claim against the said estate; 

And further, that you certify the result of the trial so had in the premises into our said orphans' court. 

WITNESS the Honorable 

President Judge of the

Orphans' Court of Philadelphia County, this of in the year of our Lord one thousand nine hundred and day 

Clerk of Orphans' Court.

Let the within precept issue. J. M.

O. SALES UNDER THE REVISED PRICE ACT 1. Requirements of the Petition 

(See the Act of 1917, P. L. 388.)

The Technical details incident to the preparation of the petition are also in many counties regulated by rule of court. 

In practically every jurisdiction the following matters are required in the petition: (1) Recital of the party petitioning showing his interest in the estate, how acquired, and the jurisdiction of the court. (2) Recital of the provisions of the will (if any) relating to the property, a complete copy of the will being annexed as an exhibit.

DECEDENTS' ESTATES 

(3) Description of the property in detail with recital of title. into the decedent. (4) Recital of all parties in interest with their status (as to minority, etc.) and the nature of their interests. (5) If a private sale a recital as to the terms of the sale and the party vendee. (6) Averment that the proposed sale will be to the interest and advantage of the estate. (7) Statement of valuation verified usually by affidavits of at least two real estate experts not interested in the transaction, annexed as exhibits. (8) A showing as to officially assessed valuation accompanied by a certificate from the proper authority annexed as an exhibit. (9) Statement where necessary giving the facts as to the physical condition of the property and why the proposed sale will benefit the estate. (10) Statement as to joinder of parties and their agreement that the sale is advantageous. (11) Statement as to the reason for invoking the jurisdiction of the court, the relief desired, and the effect of the sale in the language of the statute. (12) Prayer for leave to sell or mortgage, etc., as the case may be, carefully drawn to follow as closely as possible the language of the decree. (13) Signature and affidavit by petitioner. (14) Joinder by all parties in interest, minors, by guardians, lunatics, etc., by committees, etc. (15) Exhibits as above set forth. (16) A form of decree which should be carefully drawn and should follow as closely as possible the language of the prayer of the petition.

Certain of the above requirements will of course be omitted where the sale is to be a public one. 

Where all parties do not join the prayer will be for a citation on those not concurring to show cause why the sale or mortgage should not be allowed or confirmed as the case may be. 

The provisions of the act hereinbefore set forth—apply alike to public and private sales, though the latter are much the more numerous.

DECLARATORY JUDGMENTS 

The Act of June 18, 1923, P. L. 840, gives Courts of record within their respective jurisdictions, power to declare rights, status, and other legal relations whether or not further relief is or could be claimed. No action or proceeding shall be open

DECLARATORY JUDGMENTS 

to objection on the ground that a declaratory judgment or decree is prayed for. The declaration may be either affirmative or negative in form and effect, and such declarations shall have the force and effect of a final judgment or decree. 

Any person interested under a deed, will, written contract or other writing, constituting a contract, or whose rights, status, or other legal relations, are affected by a statute, municipal ordinance, contract or franchise, may have determined any question of construction or validity arising thereunder, and obtain a declaration of rights, status, or other legal relations thereunder. Jurisdiction under the act will never be assumed unless an actual controversy or the ripening seeds of one exist. 

The prime purpose of the act is to render practical help in ending controversies which threaten to result in litigation but where other relief is not immediately available, or where established forms of action will not immediately afford the required relief. 

A declaratory judgment cannot properly be given where another established remedy is available for prompt relief. 

For a review of the cases under the act, see Cryan's Estate, 301 Pa. 386.

C., the then owner of the said premises, and the said respondent, C. H. L., dated June 26, 1911. A true copy of said lease, marked "Exhibit A" is hereunto annexed and made part hereof. L., entered into the possession of said premises under the said lease, and at the end or expiration of the period of ten years from July 1, 1911, remained in the possession of said premises, and has continued, and still continues, to remain in the possession thereof, paying the same rent as theretofore.

DEEDS AND RECITALS SEE ACKNOWLEDGMENTS;  

A DEED is a writing or instrument, under seal, containing some contract or agreement, and which has been delivered by the parties. In its more confined sense, it is a writing by which lands, tenements, and hereditaments are conveyed, which writing is sealed and delivered by the parties. 

In some deeds covenants are inserted to oblige the parties, or one of them, to do something beneficial to, or to abstain from something, which, if done, might be prejudicial to the other. 

The following are essentials in making a deed, viz: 1st. It must be written or printed on parchment or paper. Typewriting is valid. Act 18 June, 1895. 2d. The parties must be properly qualified. 3d. There must be a proper subject-matter, which is the object of the grant. 4th. A sufficient consideration. 5th. An agreement properly set forth. 6th. It must have been read to the party executing it, if desired. 7th. It must be signed and sealed. 8th. It must be delivered; and 9th, attested by witnesses. Subscribing witnesses are not essential. 10th. It should be properly acknowledged before a competent officer; and 11th, it ought to be recorded upon delivery. 

A deed may be avoided, 1st. By alterations made in it after its execution. 2d. By the disagreement of those parties whose concurrence is necessary. 3d. By the judgment of a competent tribunal. 

A written scroll enclosing the word "seal," or "L. S.," is a good and valid seal in Pennsylvania. See Lorah v. Nisley, 156

Pa. 329.

The consideration for the execution of a deed, which, as above stated, must be sufficient, may be either a good or a valuable one. A good consideration is such as that of blood, or natural love and affection, as when a man grants an estate to a near relation being founded on motives of generosity, prudence, or natural duty. A valuable consideration is such as money, marriage, or the like, which the law esteems an equivalent given for the grant, and is therefore founded in motives of justice. Deeds made upon good consideration only, are considered as merely voluntary, and are frequently set aside in favor of creditors and bona fide purchasers.

If the grantor has a wife, she must sign and acknowledge the deed; otherwise she may, after the death of her husband, claim her dower, during her natural life. 

By the Act of 8 June, 1893, a married woman may acquire and dispose of her property as if she were unmarried; but she may not convey or mortgage her real estate unless her husband join. 

Under the Act of 1 April, 1909, separate acknowledgment by a wife is no longer necessary.

By the Act of 3 June, 1911, P. L. 631, a married woman may convey her real estate to her husband. 

If there be interlineations or erasures in a deed, there should be a note made of them, which should be witnessed by the witnesses.

A Warranty Deed is so called, because in such deeds the grantor covenants or undertakes to insure and defend such lands and tenements from such person and to the extent therein specified. The warranty may be general or special. It is general when it warrants against all persons, and special when it warrants only against the grantor, his heirs, and those claiming under him. The old rule was, in case the grantee having a warranty deed should be evicted, in case of eviction by title paramount, that the warrantor should give him lands of equal value; in lieu of that, the consideration money and interest are now recovered; and covenants may be inserted in a deed to make the grantor liable to a still greater extent. 

Deeds by Executors, Administrators, or Guardians, are made in an official capacity, either by powers conferred by a will, or by an order of the Orphans' Court.

A Quitclaim Deed is a release or acquittal of a person's in-

terest, whatever that may be, from all claims which the releasor has against the land therein specified. 

A Deed Poll or a Single Deed is much like a Quitclaim Deed, being made by one party only (e. g., a Sheriff's Deed). It was not indented, but polled or shaved quite even; hence its name. 

Purchasers at a judicial sale should investigate the title of property so sold, since the title conveyed can only be to the extent of the interest of the party whose interest is thus sold, excepting in sales for unpaid taxes, which always bar an adverse title. 

Deeds in Trust are given to persons to hold in fee simple, or otherwise, for the use of some other person or persons. The person holding the title is called the Trustee. The estate so held is not subject to the judgment debts of the trustee, to the dower of his wife, or the curtesy of the husband of a female trustee. 

The one for whose use the trust is created is entitled to proceeds, profits, or use.

The several parts of a common warranty deed are designated as follows: 

1st. The premises, in the first form given below, comprised in that portion extending from the commencement to (1), which contains the date; the names and descriptions of the parties; the consideration; the receipt of the same; the grant; the full description of the thing granted; the exceptions, if any; and the recitals, giving the chain of title, &c. 

2d. The habendum, in the form just referred to, comprised in that portion extending from (1) to (2), which is a statement of what estate or interest is granted by the deed. 

3d. The warranty, in the form referred to, extending from (2) to (3), by which the grantor warrants the title to the grantee.

A deed before it can be recorded must have attached thereto, and made part thereof, a certificate by the grantee or someone on his behalf setting forth the precise residence of the grantee named in the deed and this certificate must be recorded with the deed.

26. Deed of Trust for the Sole and Separate Use of a Married Woman 

(A separate use trust can be created only for a woman married or in contemplation of immediate marriage. The deed is usually made to a trustee for the sole and separate use of the wife. However, it is not the less a separate use estate because the deed is made directly to the wife. 

If no trustee be named, equity will raise one to effectuate the grantor's intention. A clear intention to establish a sole and separate use trust must appear.

SEPARATE USE 

1237 The wife's power over the sole and separate use property depends entirely upon the terms of the instrument. A separate use trust gives a wife the power to convey and mortgage, through the trustee, property without the joinder of her husband, free and clear of curtesy.) (Use same form as number one and add following after the habendum clause:)

In Trust, nevertheless, for the sole and separate use of my daughter Catharine wife of Charles her heirs and assigns forever, free and discharged from any and all control of her said husband and of any curtesy or other interest therein on his part, with power to the said trustee to manage, let and demise the said premises hereby granted and conveyed, to receive and collect the rents and profits therefrom, and after payment of all charges thereon, to pay over the net income to the said Catharine or to such person as she shall, in writing appoint; and with further power to said. trustee to sell and convey, any part of the aforesaid persons, and for such sum in fee simple, the whole or premises, to any person or or sums of money as the said Catharine by writ- ing under her hand and seal, and duly acknowledged at anytime during her lifetime, or by her last will and testament, may appoint and direct.

29. Spendthrift Trust Deed 

(A peculiar feature of the Pennsylvania law of trusts is the doctrine by which an estate for life can be made nontransferable and free from the owner's debts. The trust must be an active one. The instrument creating such an estate must name a trustee (267 Pa. 207). A spendthrift trust cannot be created by a grantor for himself (218 Pa. 207).) (Use same form as number one and add following after the habendum clause):

IN TRUST, however, to collect and receive the rents, income and profits from the said premises and after paying therefrom and thereon the taxes, water rents, costs of repairs and all other necessary charges, including a commission of 5% to the trustee, to apply so much of the net income as in the judgment of the trustee shall be proper to the support and maintainence of John Doe, so long as he may live, free and discharged from liability to execution or attachment in any form for any debts or liabilities whatsoever of said John Doe or to assignment or anticipation in any manner by the said John Doe and upon the further trust, upon the death of said John Doe to convey said premises and the funds in possession of said trustee to such person or persons as the said John Doe by his last will and testament in writing duly executed shall appoint, and in default of such appointment the trustee shall convey said premises and whatever funds which may then remain in the said trust to the person or persons entitled to receive the same under the intestate laws of the state of Pennsylvania, as if the said John Doe had died seized thereof in fee.

42. Recitals to Be Used in Deeds, etc. 

A RECITAL is the repetition of some former writing, or the statement of something which has been done. Touchst. 76.

Recitals are used to explain those matters of fact which are necessary to make the transaction intelligible. 2 Bl. Com. 298.

Thus, in a deed, it is frequently necessary to recite certain matters connected with the title, for the purpose of explaining its derivation.

DEPOSITIONS, COMMISSIONS AND LETTERS ROGATORY 

A DEPOSITION is the testimony of a witness reduced to writing in due form of law, taken by virtue of a commission or other authority of a competent tribunal. 

Rules of court generally provide that either party may at any time enter a rule to take the depositions of witnesses, upon reasonable notice to the opposite party. 

The rule to take testimony of aged, infirm or going witnesses

DEPOSITIONS, COMMISSIONS, LETTERS ROGATORY 

is usually entered of course; in other cases generally a rule to show cause is required.

By provision of the Act of 25 June, 1895, P. L. 279, a twentyday rule may be taken (as of course) to take depositions of witnesses beyond the limits of the Commonwealth and within 100 miles of the courthouse. 

By an Act of Assembly of Pennsylvania of the 26th February, 1831, in all cases where a deposition is to be taken upon a commission, or on a rule of court, or of a Justice of the Peace, the individual authorized to take the deposition may issue a subpœna for any witness named, and compel his attendance by attachment, or commit him to prison if he refuses to testify. 

Where a witness resides beyond the limits of the state, a commission may be issued upon interrogatories filed. Act of 1911, P. L. 709.

A notice to take depositions should have sufficient certainty, as to time, and place, to enable the opposite party to attend without any extraordinary search. The hours between which a deposition is to be taken, must be named, and it cannot legally be taken at any other time, unless by consent of the parties, which should be made to appear. 

A deposition taken in pursuance of a rule of court cannot be read in evidence, unless it appear by the certificate of the Justice that it was taken at the time and place mentioned in the notice. 

At the time and place named in the notice, the witness, before his deposition is taken, should be sworn or affirmed to declare the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. The deposition should be written by the commissioner appointed to take it, or by the witness himself, or by one not interested in the matter in dispute, who is properly authorized by the commissioner.

When a deposition is taken before a Justice on interrogatories, it is the duty of the Justice to put the interrogatories severally to the witness, and to obtain distinct answers to each. 

A deposition taken before a Justice under a rule, ought to be reduced to writing, from the mouth of the witnesses in the presence of the Justice.

A deposition should be signed by the witness and by the commissioner; when the witness cannot write, it should be so stated, and he should affix his mark or cross.

COMMISSIONS 

If a party wishes to procure the testimony of witnesses beyond the limits of the state, a rule must be taken upon interrogatories filed, and a commission for that purpose issued. Some variation exists in the rules of court relative thereto, in the several Judicial Districts of this Commonwealth. The following forms will answer for most of the Districts, and for the remainder changes can be made to suit their practice. 

Any competent person may be appointed a commissioner. 

Justices of the Peace are also empowered to issue commissions to take depositions to be read in causes depending before them. 

A Register of Wills has like power.

DEPOSITIONS, COMMISSIONS, LETTERS ROGATORY 

First cross-interrogatory.—What is your age, occupation, and residence? and state also how long you have been engaged in your present occupation, and how long you have resided at your present residence? 

Second cross-interrogatory.-Do you know the in this suit? If so, state how and when you became acquainted with him.

Third cross-interrogatory.-[Frame questions to ascertain whether the witness is in any way interested or prejudiced in favor of the party for whom he testifies.] 

Fourth cross-interrogatory.-If in any of your answers you profess to give or refer to any declaration or conversation of any of the parties, state particularly when and where it took place and who were present, and where the person or persons so present are now to be found or were to be found at your last knowledge of them. 

Fifth cross-interrogatory.-In every instance in which you state a fact, mention from whom you derived your information or heard what you state, at what time or times, and whether it has been since the institution of this suit; give all the sources and particulars of your knowledge, and state also whether you have any written memoranda of the circumstances, persons, places, or dates to which you refer in your answer; and if so, annex the said memoranda to your deposition. 

Sixth cross-interrogatory.—If in your answer to any of the interrogatories you annex or refer to any paper, letter, or document, state particularly from whom, when, where, and by what authority you become possessed of the same. 

Seventh cross-interrogatory—If after reading or hearing read to you the cross-interrogatories which follow the present cross-interrogatory, you know or can recollect any other matter or thing which is or may be material or of advantage to the party filing the cross-interrogatories, and which is not responsive to the foregoing or to the succeeding cross-interrogatories, please state the said

LETTERS ROGATORY

DEPUTATION SEE CONSTABLES; SHERIFFS DEPUTATION is the act by which a substitute or representative is appointed.

A DEPUTY is one authorized by an officer to exercise the office or right which said officer possesses, for and in place of the latter. In general, ministerial officers can appoint deputies, but where the office partakes of a judicial as well as ministerial character, although a deputation may be made for ministerial acts, one cannot be made to authorize the performance of a ju-

DETINUE 

dicial act; thus, a sheriff cannot appoint a deputy to hold an inquisition under a writ of inquiry, though he may to serve a writ. In general, a deputy has power to do every act which his principal might do, but he cannot appoint a deputy. A deputy should always act in the name of his principal, who is liable for the deputy's acts, performed by him as such, and for the neglect of the deputy. And the deputy is liable himself, to the person injured, for his own tortious acts.
